## Load recruitment data
This is downloaded from REDcap with Recruitment event selected ("recruitment_arm_1" arm)

rec_data <- read_csv("../../REACH Baseline Data Cleaning/Data/REACH_recruitment_data_4-1-2026.csv") %>% 
  dplyr::select(
    record_id,
    source,
    othsource,
    prov

    study_id = paste0("REACH", str_pad(record_id, width = 4, pad = "0"))) %>%

      source == 1 ~ "Reddit - R/IBS",
      source == 2 ~ "Facebook Ad",

Network Newsletter",

      source == 5 ~ "Health Care Provider",

## Renaming and recoding variables
```{r}
alldata <- alldata |>
  rename(
    child_age = bqp2,
    child_sex = dqp3,
    parent_age = bqp4,
    parent_sex = bqp5,
    parent_eth = bqp10,
    child_eth = bqp13,
    num_ppl_household = bqp16,
    num_child_household = bqp17,
    parent_edu = bqp19,
    parent_work = bqp20,
    relationstatus = bqp23,
    partner_edu = bqp24,
    partner_work = bqp25,
    child_daycare_time = bqp29,
    child_othercg_time = bqp30,
    # leave insurance type alone for now
    household_income = bqp37,
    language_notEnglish = bqp38,
    English_fluency = bqp39
  ) |>
  mutate( # combine vars that have other, write in responses
    relationchild = ifelse(bqp8=="Other, write here:", bqp9, bqp8),
    notwork_reason = ifelse(bqp21=="Other, write here:", bqp22, bqp21),
    partner_notwork_reason = ifelse(bqp26=="Other, write here:", "other", bqp26),
    child_outsidecare = case_when(
      bqp28___1	== "Checked" & bqp28___2	== "Unchecked" ~ "Yes, at school or daycare",
      bqp28___1	== "Checked" & bqp28___2	== "Checked" ~ "Yes, at school/daycare and with other caregivers",
      bqp28___1	== "Unchecked" & bqp28___2	== "Checked" ~ "Yes, with other caregivers",
      bqp28___3	== "Checked" ~ "No"
    ),
    partner_pain = case_when(
      mh21___1	== "Checked" ~ 1,
      mh21___1	== "Unchecked" ~ 0
    ),
    grandparents_pain = case_when(
      mh21___2	== "Checked" ~ 1,
      mh21___2	== "Unchecked" ~ 0
    ),
    sitters_pain = case_when(
      mh21___3	== "Checked" ~ 1,
      mh21___3	== "Unchecked" ~ 0
    ),
    siblings_pain = case_when(
      mh21___4	== "Checked" ~ 1,
      mh21___4	== "Unchecked" ~ 0
    ),
    auntuncle_pain = case_when(
      mh21___5	== "Checked" ~ 1,
      mh21___5	== "Unchecked" ~ 0
    ),
    others_pain = case_when(
      mh21___6	== "Checked" ~ 1,
      mh21___6	== "Unchecked" ~ 0
    ),
    ql_source = case_when(
      ql_source == 2 ~ "Toddler",
      ql_source == 1 ~ "Young_Child"
    ),
    # make binary education variables for use in analyses
    parent_college = ifelse(parent_edu == "Bachelors degree" | parent_edu == "Graduate degree (e.g., Master, Doctoral)", 1, 0),
    parent_graddeg = ifelse(parent_edu == "Graduate degree (e.g., Master, Doctoral)", 1, 0),
    # recode prefer not to respond to NA for ethnicity to get binary var for testing
    parent_eth_bin = ifelse(parent_eth == "Prefer not to respond", NA, parent_eth)
  )
```

## Partner without chronic pain variable
```{r}
test <- alldata |>
  dplyr::select(study_id, relationstatus, contains("_pain"), num_ppl_household, num_child_household, num_biocare_pain) %>% 
  mutate(
    num_adults_household = num_ppl_household - num_child_household,
    coparent_status = case_when(
      relationstatus=="Married/Living with Partner" & partner_pain == 0 ~ "coparent_nopain",
      relationstatus=="Married/Living with Partner" & partner_pain == 1 ~ "coparent_pain",
      relationstatus!="Married/Living with Partner" & partner_pain == 1 ~ "check",
      relationstatus!="Married/Living with Partner" & partner_pain == 0 ~ "no_coparent"),
    # if they have partner they indicated has pain but they don't live together
    coparent_status = ifelse(coparent_status=="check" & num_adults_household == 1, "no_coparent", coparent_status),
    # final person with 'check' is divorced but partner has pain and living with another adult -- NA
    coparent_status = ifelse(coparent_status=="check" & num_adults_household>=1, NA, coparent_status)
  )

# this in imperfect bc there are people who are living with other adults in househodl with no_coparent status
cases <- test %>% 
  dplyr::filter(coparent_status == "no_coparent" & num_adults_household > 1)

# 3 of these have nobody else in household with pain: 2 of them have grandparents with pain, 1 has sibling with pain
# some of these could be adult children? 

# count number with partner pain
test %>% dplyr::count(coparent_status) # 104 with coparent no pain, 55 with coparent pain 
```
There are 3 people who said their partner has pain but didn't indicate they were married/living with partner. Two of those said that there is 1 adult in the household, so can put those as "no_coparent". The third person said they were divorced but also that there were 2 adults in household. So for that person, will recode coparent_status to be NA (unclear if partner is living in household or not)

## Recode IBS-SSS for those who said no to first question and rescore IBS-SSS
So the follow-up question responses are 0 instead of NA
```{r}
# recode 
alldata <- alldata |>
  mutate(
    # how severe is your abdominal pain? recode to 0 people who said no
    ibs1b = ifelse(ibs1a == 0, 0, ibs1b),
    # how many days out of 10 do you get abdominal pain? use var recoded to 0-100 scale
    ibs1cr = ifelse(ibs1a == 0, 0, ibs1cr),
    # recode to 0 people who said no 
    ibs2b = ifelse(ibs2a == 0, 0, ibs2b)
    # recode people who looks like left the slider at default (50) -- did not do this bc Hafsah said data quality check confirmed those ps missed that Q
    #ibs2b = ifelse(ibs2a == 1 & is.na(ibs2b), 50, ibs2b)
  )

# study ids for those who have ibs2a = 1 but NA for ibs2b
alldata$study_id[alldata$ibs2a == 1 & is.na(alldata$ibs2b)] # highest is 477

# rescore
# create number missing var
# if number missing less than or equal to 1, rowmean * 5

alldata <- alldata |>
  mutate(
    ibs_miss = rowSums(is.na(across(all_of(c("ibs1b", "ibs1cr", "ibs2b", "ibs3", "ibs4"))))),
    ibs_tot_re = ifelse(ibs_miss < 2, rowMeans(across(all_of(c("ibs1b", "ibs1cr", "ibs2b", "ibs3", "ibs4"))), na.rm=TRUE) * 5, NA),
    ibs_cat_re = case_when(
      ibs_tot_re < 75 ~ "little to no symptom severity",
      ibs_tot_re >= 75 & ibs_tot_re < 175 ~ "mild IBS symptoms",
      ibs_tot_re >= 175 & ibs_tot_re < 300 ~ "moderate IBS symptoms",
      ibs_tot_re >= 300 ~ "severe IBS symptoms"
    )
  )

check <- alldata |>
  select(study_id, contains("ibs"), ibs_tot, ibs_tot_re, ibs_cat, ibs_cat_re)

# 244, 270 are given score with this but not from Kristen's -- thse 2 look like they're only missing 1 item so keep with the ibs_tot_re for now
```

## Clean pain duration
A few people put number of years greater than their age
REACH0271 - parent age is 4 (??) --> decided to ask parent again for age; until hear back, replace with NA
REACH0212 - put duration of fibro 115 (probably 15, very inconsistent responses across timepoints) --> decided to replace with NA
REACH0619 - put duratino migraine 48 when age is 41 (probably 12) --> decided to swap 48 for 12
REACH1042 - put duration of abdominal pain as 2018. Going to assume means started experiencing in 2018 --> 8 years
```{r}
# generate flag to dx the issues
test <- alldata %>% 
  dplyr::select(study_id, parent_age, contains("dur_"), pain_duration) %>% 
  mutate(paindur_flag = ifelse(pain_duration > parent_age, 1, 0))

# implement decisions described above
alldata[alldata$study_id == "REACH0212", "pain_duration"] <- NA
alldata[alldata$study_id == "REACH0619", "pain_duration"] <- 12
alldata[alldata$study_id == "REACH0271", "parent_age"] <- NA
alldata[alldata$study_id == "REACH1042", "pain_duration"] <- 8 
```

## CSSI scoring notes
If equal-interval scores are preferred, the Rasch measure scores may be used rather than the CSSI-8 total sum scores. Rasch measure scores corresponding to each CSSI-8 total score appear in a lookup table in Supplementary Materials File S1. Percentile scores are also provided and may enable clinicians to compare their patients to those in the n = 876 clinic sample from this study (8-18 years, tertiary care pediatric GI clinic). (from: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11593210/)

## Bivariate associations
Pearson's r, t-test, ANOVA, chi-square test
categorical variables: education (binary), birth order (binary), language (binary), white/poc (binary), nih race (multicat)

To get the corrplot sig stars to appear above the numbers:
you have to re-do this step everytime you newly loaded the corrplot package) solution:
Change the place_points function within the corrplot function. To do so, run:

trace(corrplot, edit=TRUE)

Then replace on line 443

place_points = function(sig.locs, point) {
  text(pos.pNew[, 1][sig.locs], pos.pNew[, 2][sig.locs], 
       labels = point, col = pch.col, cex = pch.cex, 
       lwd = 2)
with:

place_points = function(sig.locs, point) {
      text(pos.pNew[, 1][sig.locs], (pos.pNew[, 2][sig.locs])+0.25, 
           labels = point, col = pch.col, cex = pch.cex, 
           lwd = 2)
           
and then hit the "Save" button.
```{r}
# add peqdsql vars
all_contvars <- alldata |>
  dplyr::select(income_to_needs, r_coi_nat, z_coi_nat, arcsp_tot, phq_tot, gad_tot, pcs_tot, mspss_tot, ibs_tot_re, dpfreq_tot, total_hh_pain, parent_age, contains("ql_"), -ql_source, cssi_tot, panaspa)

# correlations between continuous variables
cont_vars_corrplot <- all_contvars |> drop_na()

M1 = cor(cont_vars_corrplot)
testRes1 = cor.mtest(cont_vars_corrplot, conf.level = 0.95)

corrplot(M1, p.mat = testRes1$p,
         sig.level = 0.05, order = 'hclust', addrect = 2, type = "lower") 

corrplot(M1,
         method="color",
         type="lower",
         order="hclust",
         addrect=2,
         diag=TRUE,
         p.mat = testRes1$p,
         insig = "label_sig",
         sig.level = .05,
         pch.cex = 0.8,
         number.cex=0.6, # change size of numbers in boxes
         pch.col = "red",
         tl.col="black",
         tl.cex=0.6,
         addCoef.col = "black",
         tl.pos="lt",
         cl.pos="r",
         outline=TRUE)

stats::cor.test(cont_vars_corrplot$arcsp_tot, cont_vars_corrplot$r_coi_nat)

# t-test with pairs of cont and binary variables: education (college and grad, binary), birth order (binary), language (binary), white/poc (binary)
# cont vars to test: r_coi_nat, protectiveness, pain catastrophizing, parenting hassles frequency, social support, ibs symptoms
t.test(r_coi_nat ~ parent_college, data=alldata) # sig, higher COI in college-educated
t.test(r_coi_nat ~ parent_graddeg, data=alldata) # sig, higher COI with grad deg 
t.test(r_coi_nat ~ oldest_child, data=alldata) # ns (as expected)
t.test(r_coi_nat ~ language_notEnglish, data=alldata) # ns
t.test(r_coi_nat ~ parent_race_bi, data=alldata) # ns
t.test(r_coi_nat ~ parent_eth_bin, data=alldata) # ns

t.test(arcsp_tot ~ parent_college, data=alldata) # sig, college-educated less protective
t.test(arcsp_tot ~ parent_graddeg, data=alldata) # sig, grad-degree less protective
t.test(arcsp_tot ~ oldest_child, data=alldata) # ns
t.test(arcsp_tot ~ language_notEnglish, data=alldata) # ns
t.test(arcsp_tot ~ parent_race_bi, data=alldata) # ns
t.test(arcsp_tot ~ parent_eth_bin, data=alldata) # ns

t.test(pcs_tot ~ parent_college, data=alldata) # ns
t.test(pcs_tot ~ parent_graddeg, data=alldata) # ns
t.test(pcs_tot ~ language_notEnglish, data=alldata) # ns
t.test(pcs_tot ~ parent_race_bi, data=alldata) # ns

t.test(ibs_tot ~ parent_college, data=alldata) # sig, college-educated lower IBS severity
t.test(ibs_tot ~ parent_graddeg, data=alldata) # sig
t.test(ibs_tot ~ language_notEnglish, data=alldata) # ns
t.test(ibs_tot ~ parent_race_bi, data=alldata) # ns

t.test(mspss_tot ~ parent_college, data=alldata) # sig. college-educated more social support
t.test(mspss_tot ~ parent_graddeg, data=alldata) # sig, grad-degree more social support
t.test(mspss_tot ~ language_notEnglish, data=alldata) # ns
t.test(mspss_tot ~ parent_race_bi, data=alldata) # ns

t.test(dpfreq_tot ~ parent_college, data=alldata) # ns
t.test(dpfreq_tot ~ parent_graddeg, data=alldata) # ns
t.test(dpfreq_tot ~ language_notEnglish, data=alldata) # ns 
t.test(dpfreq_tot ~ parent_race_bi, data=alldata) # POC report less frequent parenting hassles

t.test(income_to_needs ~ parent_college, data=alldata) # sig

# ANOVA with multicategorical variable: NIH race
summary(aov(r_coi_nat~parent_race_nih, data=alldata)) # sig

race_comp_data <- alldata |> # filter out the race categories that only occur once, so that the t-test can be run
  dplyr::filter(parent_race_nih != "American Indian/AK Native" & parent_race_nih != "Native Hawaiian/other Pac. Isl.")

pairwise.t.test(race_comp_data$r_coi_nat, race_comp_data$parent_race_nih, p.adj = "BH") # Black parents lower COI than other races

summary(aov(arcsp_tot~parent_race_nih, data=alldata)) # ns
summary(aov(pcs_tot~parent_race_nih, data=alldata)) # ns
summary(aov(ibs_tot~parent_race_nih, data=alldata)) # ns
summary(aov(mspss_tot~parent_race_nih, data=alldata)) # ns
summary(aov(dpfreq_tot~parent_race_nih, data=alldata)) # ns
summary(aov(phq_tot~parent_race_nih, data=alldata)) # ns
summary(aov(gad_tot~parent_race_nih, data=alldata)) #ns

# chi-square tests: education and race
edu_race_chisq <- chisq.test(race_comp_data$parent_race_nih, race_comp_data$parent_college) # sig
observed_counts <- edu_race_chisq$observed
expected_counts <- edu_race_chisq$expected

# Calculate contribution to chi-square statistic
contributions <- (observed_counts - expected_counts)^2 / expected_counts

# Calculate percentage contributions
total_chi_square <- edu_race_chisq$statistic
percentage_contributions <- 100 * contributions / total_chi_square

# Print percentage contributions
print("Percentage Contributions:")
print(round(percentage_contributions, 2)) # more Black lower educated than expected
```

         method="color",
